AssignIn.description:
REQ-7. The people the request is put with; `version` guards a change of staff on a request
that is already Assigned against a second admin doing the same.
AssignIn.title: AssignIn

AtIn.description: The time something happened, as the device saw it. The server's now when absent.
AtIn.title: AtIn

stations.description: XLSX workbook, stations CSV, or the existing system's site export (JSON)
stations.title: Stations

CalibrationIn.description: A calibration recorded outside a visit (CAL-1); field checks come with visits.
CalibrationIn.title: CalibrationIn

CommentIn.description:
REQ-9, REQ-10. `id` is made on the device: sending it again returns the comment already
posted. Files are PDFs uploaded for `comment:<request id>:<id>` and already checked.
CommentIn.title: CommentIn

CommentPatch.description: Change a comment within 15 minutes: its text, and for staff whether it is internal.
CommentPatch.title: CommentPatch

ConfigDiff.description: CFG-3: which files differ between two versions, by name and checksum.
ConfigDiff.title: ConfigDiff

DocumentIn.description: Made on the device or form with its own ID, so a retry creates nothing twice.
DocumentIn.title: DocumentIn

DownloadOut.description: A link that works for ten minutes; it is never cached.
DownloadOut.title: DownloadOut

DueUnit.description: A row of the calibration-due list (CAL-4).
DueUnit.title: DueUnit

InstalledUnit.description: STN-4: model, serial, install date, last calibration and calibration due.
InstalledUnit.title: InstalledUnit

Override.description: VIS-6: a station ended without a Before or After image, with the reason (W12).
Override.title: Override

Places.description: The form's time zone choices: each country's IANA zones, from `tzdata` (W5-7).
Places.title: Places

QrResolved.description: What a scanned label points at (QR-2, QR-3). `view` picks the page the app opens.
QrResolved.title: QrResolved

QueueItem.description: A row of the queue: a request and how long it has waited.
QueueItem.title: QueueItem

RequestIn.description:
REQ-1, REQ-2. `id` is made on the device (rule 9): sending the same one again returns
the request already made instead of a second one. An admin names the `org_id` (every
station must be that organization's); a client's is their own.
RequestIn.title: RequestIn

RequestPatch.description: REQ-11. Only what is sent changes. `version` is the one the editor was looking at.
RequestPatch.title: RequestPatch

RequestSummary.description: A row of the request list (AFD `/requests`).
RequestSummary.title: RequestSummary

Resolved.description: What a visit to this station is given (W10-11).
Resolved.title: Resolved

Spec.description:
One line of a model's technical specifications: `Operating range: -80 to +60 °C`, with an
optional second line (`0 to 100 % RH`). Free text: loggers and sensors have different ones.
Spec.title: Spec

StaffOut.description: Someone who may attend a visit: a name and roles, never an email or phone.
StaffOut.title: StaffOut

StationDocuments.description: What the station page's Documents tab shows: the station's own and its sensors'.
StationDocuments.title: StationDocuments

StationPatch.description: `owner_org_id` is not here: stations never change owner (BSD B5).
StationPatch.title: StationPatch

StationSummary.description: A row of the station list (DBD "Stations list").
StationSummary.title: StationSummary

TemplatePatch.description: `version` is the version the editor was looking at: if someone saved a newer one, 409.
TemplatePatch.title: TemplatePatch

VisitBrief.description: A visit as the request page lists it.
VisitBrief.title: VisitBrief

VisitIn.description:
Scheduling (VIS-1). `id` is made on the device and makes a retry safe (rule 9): the same
`id` again returns the visit that was made.
VisitIn.title: VisitIn

VisitPatch.description:
A planned visit: any of these. A started visit: only `stations[].owner_staff_id`. What is
left out stays as it is; `notes: null` clears the notes.
VisitPatch.title: VisitPatch

WorkIn.description: The record whole, with the version the editor was looking at.
WorkIn.title: WorkIn

WorkOut.description: A station's work record as staff see it. Clients never get one (rule 6).
WorkOut.title: WorkOut

Workload.description: Open requests per person (staff IDs not listed have none).
Workload.title: Workload

get.description: Newest first. `station_id` lists what was calibrated while at that station.

post.description:
CAL-1. The unit's last calibration and due date follow the newest record (CAL-3); a
failed one flags the unit for follow-up (CAL-6). A certificate is a PDF the person already
uploaded for this unit (`calibration:<unit id>`) that has passed media's checks.

get.description: CAL-4: units overdue or due within `within_days`, overdue first.
The current version of each template. Inactive ones too, for an admin who asks (`all`).

post.description: A new template for a station type, or an add-on for a sensor model.

get.description:
What a visit to this station is given: its type's template, then an add-on for each
sensor model installed there.
The current version, or an older one by number (what a visit copied).

patch.description: Save the next version (name, items, or active). Nothing changed writes nothing.

get.description:
DOC-1, DOC-2. A client sees the current, client-visible, clean documents of their own
stations and of the models installed there. Staff see every version when `current=false`.

parameters.description: Only the newest version of each
parameters.name: current

schema.description: Only the newest version of each
schema.title: Current

post.description:
DOC-3. Idempotent by `id`: a retry returns the document it made. `supersedes_id` makes
this a new version; the earlier one stays downloadable by staff.

patch.description:
Change the details of a document, or who may see it (DOC-4). The file itself never
changes: upload a new version instead.

get.description:
Check access, then ask media for a ten-minute link (model documents have no
organization in media, so this is the only way a client reaches them: BSD B4).

parameters.description: Open PDFs and images in the browser
parameters.name: inline

schema.description: Open PDFs and images in the browser
schema.title: Inline

get.description:
QR-2, QR-3. A revoked code answers 410 to anyone who may see its station, and 404 to
everyone else, so a client learns nothing about another organization's stations.
Everything waiting, with the filters the list has (a queue is short: no paging).

REQ-8, REQ-15: newest first. A client sees their organization's requests only; the
date range is inclusive of both days.

post.description:
REQ-1, REQ-2, REQ-4. A client's request starts Submitted; an admin's, made for an
organization, starts Approved. Sending the same `id` again returns the request that
was made (200), so a retry on a poor connection can't make a second one.

get.description: How many open requests each person has, for the Assign dialog (W9).
REQ-8: the request with its status history. A client sees their organization's only.

patch.description:
REQ-11: a client edits their own request while it is Submitted, Approved or Assigned;
an admin until it is done. Only what is sent changes.

post.description: REQ-6: Submitted to Approved. The request then joins the queue.

REQ-7: an admin puts one or more staff on an approved request (it becomes Assigned) or
changes the staff of one that is Assigned. Visits decide from Scheduled on.

REQ-11: a client cancels their own request up to Assigned; an admin any time before it
is done, with a reason from Scheduled on. Planned visits are cancelled in the same
transaction once visits exist (Phase 4).

REQ-7: a technician (or an admin) takes an approved request from the queue. Two people
claiming at once: one wins, the other is told who.

get.description: REQ-9, REQ-10: oldest first. A client gets no internal comments, and so no trace of them.

post.description:
REQ-9. Idempotent by `id`: a retry after a lost answer returns the comment already
posted (200). Files must already be clean (the page waits), and go to the organization
with the comment, or stay staff-only if the comment is internal.

patch.description:
REQ-9, REQ-10: the author changes the text within 15 minutes; staff may also mark their
comment internal (or not). Making it internal hides its files from the client again.

get.description: A client asking for an internal comment's file gets 404, as if it did not exist.

post.description: REQ-6: Submitted to Denied. The reason is required and the client sees it.

A technician lets go of their claim, or an admin unassigns everyone. With nobody left
the request returns to the queue (Assigned to Approved).

patch.description: A new default interval moves the due date of every unit that follows it (CAL-3).

post.description:
A unit enters the inventory in stock (or in repair or retired); it reaches a station
through `install`.

patch.description:
Serial and model corrections (SEN-5 review), status in or out of stock, the interval
override (CAL-3), notes. Installing and removing have their own actions.

post.description:
Put a unit in stock on a station (SEN-3). Visits do this through sensor actions
(Phase 4); this is the manual inventory change.
Take a unit off its station, with the reason, into stock, repair or retirement.

get.description: STN-5. Sorted by code; pass the last code as `after` for the next page.

post.description: STN-1. The owner organization is fixed for good (ORG-2, BSD B5).

get.description: The values the list's filters offer (STN-5).

post.description: STN-8. A dry run (the default) only reports; valid rows are imported otherwise.

get.description: Each country's time zones, for the station form (a one-zone country gets it filled in).
STN-4, STN-6: details with installed units; clients see their own stations only.
CFG-3: newest first.

schema.title: Response List Config Versions Api V1 Stations  Id  Config Versions Get

post.description:
CFG-1, CFG-2. Idempotent by `id`. Every file must be one this person uploaded for this
station and that has passed its checks; if one is still being checked the answer is a
409 `file_not_ready`, and trying again a moment later works.

get.description:
CFG-3: files added, removed or changed since `against` (default: the version before).
Version 1 compared with nothing lists every file as added.

The station page's Documents tab: its own documents and its sensors' manuals (DOC-1,
DOC-2). Only the current version of each.
SEN-3: which unit sat here, for which parameter, and when.

schema.title: Response Station Installations Api V1 Stations  Id  Installations Get

post.description: QR-7. Gives the station a new token and revokes the old one, in one transaction.

get.description: Soonest first. A client sees their organization's visits (VIS-11).

post.description:
VIS-1: the request's assigned staff or an admin plan a visit: dates, who attends (one the
lead), which of the request's stations, and who owns each. The request becomes Scheduled.
Sending the same `id` again returns the visit that was made (200).

get.description:
The visits I attend that are planned or under way, soonest first (AFD "My upcoming
visits").

The active technicians and admins to pick from when scheduling (VIS-1). Operations keeps
no copy of users (rule 1): auth answers, and only names and roles come back. Admins can list
users in auth; a technician who is assigned to the request cannot, so the list is here.
A client reads their organization's visits only; another's is not found (rule 4).

patch.description:
VIS-2, AFD J5 steps 5 and 5b. A planned visit: dates, people, lead, stations, owners and
notes. A started visit: only who owns which station, by the lead or an admin.

post.description:
VIS-2: a planned visit is cancelled; the request returns to Assigned when no other visit
is planned.

VIS-9: end the visit and say whether another is needed. If so the request goes back to
Assigned to be scheduled again; if not it waits for the visit report (Phase 6). The VIS-6
check of Before and After images arrives with media on visits (W12).
An admin brings a cancelled visit back: work was recorded on it offline (TRD §7.4).
VIS-4: attending staff start the visit; the request is In progress.
VIS-4: the station's owner records arriving there.
VIS-4: the station's owner records leaving it (after arriving).

put.description: VIS-7: the owner saves what was found and done at the station.

get.description:
The owner check on upload (TRD §3.3): may this user attach a file to this owner, and
which organization does the file then belong to? Not found for an owner that does not
exist or that a client cannot see (rule 4); forbidden for a role that may not write.

The weekly digest's list (CAL-5): the same units as the staff list, for every
organization, read by platform with its service token (rule 1).

post.description:
What a label sheet prints (QR-6): the code, name and QR token of each station, in the
order asked. Stations that do not exist are left out. Tokens never travel in events or
snapshots, so this is the only place report can read them.

get.description:
Current state for read-model backfill (TRD §8.6), shaped like the events' data.
Visits are in `site_visits`.
